summary: Shuman Chen is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. She earned her PhD at Northwestern University (~2008–2014) under doctoral supervisor Brook Ziporyn and committee member Sarah E. Fraser, and also studied under traditional teacher Wei Chueh.

Shun'ei Hirai is a Buddhist studies and Sinology scholar. He studied at Komazawa University (~1950–1954) and the University of Tokyo (~1955–1961), and later served as a professor at Komazawa University (~1965–1980).

Shunkyo Katsumata was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1932–1935). He held a post at Toyo University and served at Taisho University (~1949–1983) as professor emeritus.
Shunpei Ueyama was a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kyoto University from ~1940 to 1943 and later held a post there from ~1954 to 1984.

Shunryu Suzuki was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Komazawa University (~1926–1930) and under traditional teachers Gyokujun So-on and Ian Kishizawa. He founded the San Francisco Zen Center and the Tassajara Zen Mountain Center.

Shunsho Manabe is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at Tohoku University (~1957–1961) and held posts at Hosen Gakuen College and as a professor at Shikoku University.
Shunshō Terakawa was a scholar of Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Tokyo. He held a faculty post at Otani University from ~1966 to 2000, where he became Emeritus Professor.
Shuntaro Kondo is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed his PhD at Ryukoku University by 2011. He has served as a part-time lecturer at Ryukoku University.

Shuntaro Matsuyama was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. After studying at the University of Tokyo (~1950–1956), he held posts at Kokugakuin University, Tama Art University, and Joshibi University of Art and Design (~1974–1995, professor).
Shunzo Onoda specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed a D.Lit. at Bukkyo University in 1993 and served there as an associate professor from ~1992 to 2021.

Shuyu Kanaoka was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1948–1953). He served as an assistant professor at Toyo University (~1961–1980) and as a professor at Ryukoku University (~1980).

Shōkin Furuta was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at Shimane University. He held posts at Hokkaido University (~1952–1963) and Nihon University (~1964–1982), and served as director of Matsugaoka Bunko (~1966–2001).
Shōkō Kabutogi was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University from ~1933 to 1936. He later served as a professor at Rissho University.

Shūichi Katō was a Japanology and philosophy scholar educated at the University of Tokyo (~1940–1944). He held posts at the University of British Columbia, Free University of Berlin, Yale, Ritsumeikan, the University of Tokyo, and Sophia University.
Si Ti La is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at Acharya Nagarjuna University in 2014 under J. Sitaramamma, while also studying under multiple traditional teachers.

Sibani Dasgupta was an Indologist who studied at the University of Dhaka and under Rajendra Chandra Hazra. She earned a doctorate at the University of Calcutta in 1954 under doctoral supervisor Sushil Kumar De and committee members John Brough and Sumitra Mangesh Katre.

Sibraj Chetry works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Gauhati University under Sibnath Sarma and was taught by several scholars including D. K. Chakravarty, later serving as Lecturer of Philosophy at North Lakhimpur College.
Siegfried Goldschmidt was a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He studied under Albrecht Weber in 1864, under Rudolf von Roth (~1865–1867), and at the University of Tübingen in 1867.

Siegfried Lienhard was an Indology scholar who studied at the University of Vienna (~1943–1949). He held positions at the University of Kiel (~1962–1967) and served as professor at Stockholm University (~1967–1990).

Siglinde Dietz is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. She received her PhD from the University of Bonn in 1980 under Michael Hahn and held a post at the University of Göttingen around 1980.
